description: Cost of Thinking bench (OCTO article series, Part 1: plan-then-execute vs a step-by-step tool loop). One source: fitness_db (~100 rows per table, so result payloads stay small and any token gap is architectural, not data-driven). Questions are stratified by the number of database steps a careful analyst would take; the article's claim is that the loop's cost grows with steps (it re-sends its context every step) while the planner's stays near-flat. Ground truth computed against the local Teradata on 2026-10-16 with truth_sql. Scoring as in multi_source_bench.check_answer: a 'number' check finds a number within tol (relative, default 0.005); a 'text' check finds the string (case-insensitive). A small integer number check (1, 3, 10) is weak -- any such number in the answer satisfies it -- so every question also carries a text or a distinctive number check. 'top' questions were checked for ties; tied candidates were dropped.

tiers.control: No database step. The two architectures should cost about the same; a gap here is overhead, not architecture.
tiers.join: One query with a join; a careful agent still needs a single statement.
tiers.independent: Several independent facts. A planner can run them in parallel; a loop runs them one by one.
tiers.dependent: The second step needs the first step's result.
tiers.set_based: Answerable with one GROUP BY; an agent that thinks row-by-row iterates instead. The database lesson: think in sets.

questions.question: In two sentences, what is the difference between a primary key and a foreign key?
Name three common causes of slow SQL queries, one line each.
How many customers are in the fitness database?
What was the total sales amount (sum of sale totals) in 2023?
questions.truth_sql: SELECT SUM(TotalAmount) FROM fitness_db.Sales WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM SaleDate)=2023

questions.question: How many service tickets currently have the status 'Open'?
questions.truth_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM fitness_db.ServiceTickets WHERE Status='Open'

questions.question: Which product type has the most products in the catalogue, and how many?
questions.truth_sql: SELECT TOP 3 ProductType, COUNT(*) FROM fitness_db.Products GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC

questions.question: Which 3 customer states generated the most sales revenue (sum of sale totals), and how much did the top one generate?
questions.truth_sql: SELECT TOP 4 c.State, SUM(s.TotalAmount) FROM fitness_db.Sales s JOIN fitness_db.Customers c ON s.CustomerID=c.CustomerID GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC

questions.question: Which brand generated the most revenue from sale line items (quantity times unit price), and how much?
questions.truth_sql: SELECT TOP 3 p.Brand, SUM(d.Quantity*d.UnitPrice) FROM fitness_db.SaleDetails d JOIN fitness_db.Products p ON d.ProductID=p.ProductID GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC

questions.question: What is the average sale amount for customers located in the state NY?
questions.truth_sql: SELECT AVG(s.TotalAmount), COUNT(*) FROM fitness_db.Sales s JOIN fitness_db.Customers c ON s.CustomerID=c.CustomerID WHERE c.State='NY'

questions.question: How many customers are there, how many service tickets are still Open, and what was the total sales amount in 2023?
questions.truth_sql: COUNT(*) Customers; COUNT(*) ServiceTickets WHERE Status='Open'; SUM(TotalAmount) Sales WHERE year=2023

questions.question: What is the most expensive product and its price, and how many products have fewer than 10 units in stock?
questions.truth_sql: SELECT TOP 1 ProductName, Price FROM fitness_db.Products ORDER BY Price DESC; SELECT COUNT(*) FROM fitness_db.Products WHERE StockQuantity < 10

questions.question: How many service tickets are Closed, how many are In Progress, and what is the average number of days it took to resolve a Closed ticket?
questions.truth_sql: SELECT Status, COUNT(*) FROM fitness_db.ServiceTickets GROUP BY 1; SELECT AVG(CAST(ResolutionDate - TicketDate AS FLOAT)) FROM fitness_db.ServiceTickets WHERE Status='Closed'

questions.question: Who made the single largest sale (first and last name, and the amount), and how many service tickets does that customer have?
questions.truth_sql: SELECT TOP 1 CustomerID, TotalAmount FROM fitness_db.Sales ORDER BY TotalAmount DESC -> CustomerID 82; name and ticket count for 82

questions.question: Which customer state generated the most sales revenue, and how many customers are located in that state?
questions.truth_sql: top state by SUM(TotalAmount) -> RU; SELECT COUNT(*) FROM fitness_db.Customers WHERE State='RU'

questions.question: Which product sold the most units, how many units, and how many service tickets were raised for that product?
questions.truth_sql: SELECT TOP 1 p.ProductID, p.ProductName, SUM(d.Quantity) FROM fitness_db.SaleDetails d JOIN fitness_db.Products p ON d.ProductID=p.ProductID GROUP BY 1,2 ORDER BY 3 DESC -> 133; SELECT COUNT(*) FROM fitness_db.ServiceTickets WHERE ProductID=133

questions.question: For every product type, give the number of products and their average price.
questions.truth_sql: SELECT ProductType, COUNT(*), AVG(Price) FROM fitness_db.Products GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC
questions.truth: 20 types; e.g. Weights 16 / 184.62, Treadmill 12 / 2353.08, Functional Trainer 2 / 4749.99

questions.question: For each month of 2023, how many sales were made?
questions.truth_sql: SELECT EXTRACT(MONTH FROM SaleDate), COUNT(*) FROM fitness_db.Sales WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM SaleDate)=2023 GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
